title: Hymns, marches and what brass bands played for funerals
summary: Clark describes the old bands reading music, playing hymns from a little red book, and playing marches on the way back from the cemetery. Didn't He Ramble was played only occasionally.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Oh how often do those old brass bands play by ear? I wanted to get this straight.
Well I'll tell you I really can't answer for that. Because the bands that I used to follow they used to use music.
Did you ever play any hymns?
Well now and then they would play a hymn like if they bring a body out of a house, out of a church, they may play, Near My God To Thee or What a Friend We Have in Jesus.
Did they ever have a fast like By and By or Glory Land?

Well sometimes they would play Glory Land coming up to a house or a church. Fast and slow. No they would play that like we do when we come up to a house or church. You see but when they leave that they'd go in those packs and stay in those packs until they got to the cemetery. They didn't play no head numbers for a funeral.
But they would play head, the hymns would be by head?

Yeah well sometimes. Sometimes. Then they had a book at that time we used to call it, they used to call it a little red book. It had a lot of hymns in it, different hymns, they would use those books. You see? Like Church in the Wild, Wood and all such as that. Lead Kindly Life, they'd use those books. But the bands I don't know, they got away from it, you know, from those books. In other words a lot of them got away from the music. I hate to say it but it's true.
Yes well I wanted to get that straight to the dates on that. When did they start playing pretty ratty in the street?
Oh that's way back, that's way back. Oh that's... When they start playing ratty in the street that's... Oh I guess... I guess back in the 19th century.
Even there when they played all those arrangements on the way to the funeral, on the way to the graveyard, coming back from the graveyard they'd play ratty all the time, even in the old days.

Some would and some wouldn't. Now they're on within the excelsis, they wouldn't do that. Tuxedo, nil. They'd play sometime, you know those organizations ask you to play ratty number for them. You see? They didn't ask for it, those fellows played those marches.

Stars and stripes or whatever they were. Stars and stripes and such as National Emblem, Under Fire, Under Arms, and what's this other march now? Oh we used to play that thing. I can't say... Rifle Rangers, all such as that.
The things like Didn't He Ramble and those...
Well now and then they would play that. Now and then. But they got away from that. I haven't heard a band play that in a long, long time. They got away from that too. That's funny.
It's funny how they come and they go. They're wearing them out.
They come and they go. Now sometimes, sometimes somebody may ask for it. You see.
